variations.name: 1A · Midnight Minimal
variations.prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Generate ONE complete, polished ANIMAL ATLAS desktop software interface, wide landscape 16:10, edge-to-edge screenshot with no device, desk, room or perspective frame. The reference is a design-family starting point, not a layout to copy mechanically. This is an animal-event-driven musical instrument: retain a substantial understandable geographic map including New Zealand, separate stationary acoustic detections from satellite fixes, a selected-event provenance readout, record/play/loop controls, observed versus arrival timeline mode and a 60x replay option. Show source freshness independently from network status. No invented affiliations or logos. All illustrative examples must be labelled as design material: small footer 'Illustrative data · UI exploration'. Use sparse, accurately spelled functional text. Do not add claims of actual connected sources, and do not connect unrelated bird stations into paths. Each result must be one coherent interface, not a concept sheet. Explore Pelagic Observatory variation 1A, title 'ANIMAL ATLAS / MIDNIGHT MINIMAL'. Retain the scientific nautical character but strip almost everything back. Razor-sharp flat cartography; midnight ink ocean, dark slate land, ivory modern sans type and extremely sparse mint/coral event points. Huge Pacific-centered rectangular map is 85% of the interface, generously empty and calm; small floating selected-event receipt at top right, no permanent right sidebar, no animal illustrations or waveforms. A very shallow bottom performance dock with four small elegant rotary arcs Density, Tone, Decay, Space, minimal transport and thin time scrubber. One tiny source freshness line at top. No giant page heading. Map has subtle latitude/longitude grid but no busy bathymetric labels. This is the most disciplined, playable, minimal professional incarnation: a silent dark atlas with just enough music controls. Explore a genuinely different hierarchy from the reference, with map-first immersion and restrained information on demand.
